questions.question: Under a $(Q,r)$ policy with lot size $Q$ and reorder level $r$, an order is placed whenever the end-of-period inventory position has fallen to $r$ or below. What role does $r$ play?
options: It is the level the position is raised to by every order.
It is only the trigger; after ordering the position lies above $r$.
It is the largest number of lots allowed in one order.
It is the lowest position the system can ever reach.

questions.question: A shop must choose among the base-stock, $(s,S)$, $(T,S)$ and $(Q,r)$ inventory policies. In which situation is the $(Q,r)$ policy, with lot size $Q$ and reorder level $r$, the natural choice?
options: The stock can only be reviewed and ordered every $T$ periods.
Orders cost nothing to place, so each unit sold is reordered at once.
Each order must restore the position to one fixed target level.
The supplier only delivers in whole pallets of a fixed number of units.

questions.question: In a $(Q,r)$ inventory policy with $Q\in\{1,2,\dots\}$ and reorder level $r$, what does the parameter $Q$ fix?
options: The lot size: every order is a whole number of lots of $Q$ units.
The exact number of units in every order that is placed.
The highest position the system can have after ordering.
The number of periods that pass between two orders.

questions.question: Under a $(Q,r)$ policy in a periodic-review inventory system with lead time $l\ge1$, which quantity decides the order placed at the start of period $k$?
options: The inventory level $I_{k-1}'$ at the end of period $k-1$
The inventory position $P_{k-1}$ at the start of period $k-1$
The inventory position $P_{k-1}'$ at the end of period $k-1$
The demand $D_k$ that will occur during period $k$

questions.question: Which inventory policy is a $(Q,r)$ policy with lot size $Q=1$ and reorder level $r$, which orders $\lceil r+1-P'\rceil\mathbf{1}\{P'\le r\}$ after end position $P'$?
options: The base-stock policy with base-stock level $S=r$
The base-stock policy with base-stock level $S=r+1$
A policy that orders exactly one unit whenever $P'\le r$
A policy that orders one unit in every period

questions.question: A shop uses a $(Q,r)$ policy with lot size $Q=4$ and reorder level $r=2$: when the end-of-period inventory position is at most $r$, it orders the fewest lots needed to exceed $r$. A period ends exactly at position $2$. How many units are ordered?

Under a $(Q,r)$ policy with $Q=5$ and $r=3$, the order after end-of-period inventory position $P'\le r$ is $Q\lceil(r+1-P')/Q\rceil$. After a large demand, a period ends at $P'=-4$. How large is the order?

A $(Q,r)$ policy has lot size $Q=3$ and reorder level $r=-2$; it orders lots whenever the end-of-period inventory position is at most $r$, until the position exceeds $r$. What is the set of all inventory positions that can occur right after an order?

A shop runs a $(Q,r)$ policy with lot size $Q=4$, reorder level $r=2$ and lead time $l=2$ periods. At the end of a period the inventory level is $1$ (one unit on the shelf, no backlog) and one lot of $4$ units, ordered at the start of that period, is still on its way. How many units does the policy order at the start of the next period?

Take the order rule $Q_k=Q\lceil(r+1-P_{k-1}')/Q\rceil\,\mathbf{1}\{P_{k-1}'\le r\}$ of a $(Q,r)$ policy, with $P_{k-1}'$ the end-of-period inventory position. For $Q=4$, $r=2$ and $P_{k-1}'=8$, what does the rule give?
A $(Q,r)$ policy uses $m=\lceil(r+1-P')/Q\rceil$ lots after an end-of-period position $P'\le r$. Why is the ceiling used rather than the floor $\lfloor(r+1-P')/Q\rfloor$?
options: The ceiling makes the order $mQ$ a whole number of units.
The ceiling makes the position $P'+mQ$ return to exactly $r+Q$.
The ceiling keeps the order $mQ$ at no more than one lot of $Q$.
The ceiling makes $m$ the smallest integer with $P'+mQ\ge r+1$.

questions.question: A $(Q,r)$ policy with lot size $Q$ and reorder level $r$ places an order after an end-of-period inventory position $P'\le r$. On what does the inventory position right after ordering depend?
options: On nothing: it always equals the top level $r+Q$.
On nothing: it always equals the lowest level $r+1$.
Only on the remainder of $r-P'$ after division by $Q$.
Only on $P'$ through $P'+Q$, one lot above $P'$.

questions.question: A $(Q,r)$ policy orders $m=\lceil(r+1-P')/Q\rceil$ lots of size $Q$ after an end-of-period position $P'\le r$. Why can the position $P'+mQ$ after ordering never exceed $r+Q$?
options: Since demand is non-negative, $P'\le P_k$, so the position can only fall.
Since $m$ is minimal, $P'+(m-1)Q\le r$, so $P'+mQ\le r+Q$.
Since every order is a single lot, $P'\le r$ gives $P'+Q\le r+Q$.
Since $P'\ge r-Q$ always holds, one lot suffices, so $P'+Q\le r+Q$.

questions.question: An inventory system with a $(Q,r)=(4,2)$ policy starts period $1$ at inventory position $P_1=6$; the demands in periods $1$, $2$, $3$ are $3$, $2$, $4$. Which orders $Q_2,Q_3,Q_4$ are placed at the starts of periods $2$, $3$, $4$?

Two policies face the same end-of-period inventory position $P'=-1$: a $(Q,r)$ policy with $Q=5$, $r=1$, which orders the smallest number of lots of $5$ that lifts the position above $r$, and an $(s,S)$ policy with $s=1$, $S=6$. How much does each order?
options: Both policies order $7$ units.
Both policies order $5$ units.
$(Q,r)$ orders $10$ units and $(s,S)$ orders $7$ units.
$(Q,r)$ orders $5$ units and $(s,S)$ orders $7$ units.

questions.question: A $(Q,r)$ policy with $Q=4$ and $r=2$ keeps every start-of-period inventory position in $\{3,4,5,6\}$, and demand in a period is an integer between $0$ and $5$. Which order sizes can occur?

A $(Q,r)$ policy with lot size $Q$ and reorder level $r$ starts with inventory position $P_1=r+Q+5$, above the band $\{r+1,\dots,r+Q\}$. Which statement about the start-of-period positions $P_k$ is correct?
options: An order at the start of period $2$ brings the position down into the band.
Once some $P_k$ lies in the band, every later start position stays in it.
The position can never enter the band, because orders come in lots of $Q$.
After entering the band, a multi-lot order can lift it above $r+Q$ again.

questions.question: Compare a $(Q,r)$ policy, which orders $Q\lceil(r+1-P')/Q\rceil$ when $P'\le r$, with the $(s,S)$ policy with $s=r$ and $S=r+Q$. For which lot sizes $Q$ do the two policies place the same order after every possible end position $P'$?
options: For every $Q$, since both keep the position in $\{r+1,\dots,r+Q\}$.
For every $Q$, since both order only when $P'\le r$.
For no $Q$, since $(Q,r)$ orders are always smaller.
Only for $Q=1$, since $r-P'$ must be a multiple of $Q$.

questions.question: An unknown $(Q,r)$ policy, ordering $Q\lceil(r+1-P')/Q\rceil$ whenever the end position $P'\le r$, is observed: after $P'=0$ it orders $6$, after $P'=1$ it orders $6$, after $P'=2$ nothing, and after $P'=-5$ it orders $12$. Which parameters fit all four observations?
A $(Q,r)$ policy with $Q=4$ and $r=2$ starts at $P_1=6$, and every period's demand is $0$, $4$ or $8$ units. Which start-of-period inventory positions $P_k$ can ever occur?
options: Every level in $\{3,4,5,6\}$
The levels $2$ and $6$
Only the level $6$
The levels $-2$, $2$ and $6$
